newsitem.title: USA: U.S. DEBT FUTURES FINISH FIRM AFTER CHOPPY SESSION.
newsitem.headline: U.S. DEBT FUTURES FINISH FIRM AFTER CHOPPY SESSION.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended higher after a choppy session of heavy trading.
Debt prices quickly rallied after U.S. retail sales and producer price data were reported close to expectations, but just as quickly they crumbled from the morning's high.
The market spent the rest of the day whipsawing in nervous, technical trade.
"A lot of people didn't quite figure out what happened today," a T-bond futures trader said.
Another said there was "no rhyme or reason, really" to the market's erratic behavior.
Traders noted heavy volume during the session and said action was brisk on both downticks and recoveries.
"There was a lot of nervous trade as people were trying to square things up after this morning," a T-bond trader said.

Some traders said the market may have reacted too favorably to early U.S. data, and when highs could not be sustained, traders overcompensated on the downside. The market spent the rest of the session searching for equilibrium.
Retail sales rose 0.6 percent overall and 0.5 percent excluding autos, and producer prices fell 0.1 percent both overall and excluding food and energy.
Traders had expected a 0.1 percent gain in both producer price numbers and a 0.7 percent gain in overall retail sales.
The core retail sales rate was in line with average forecasts.
"I guess it's a little disturbing that we came off so hard after the favorable data," a T-bond trader said. "But to me it just got too high after the numbers."
Eurodollar trade turned more subdued in the afternoon, but the mood remained nervous, traders there said.
"There's not a lot of conviction from what I can tell down here," a Euro trader said.
Traders said a weak dollar exacerbated the downmoves.
"Everybody's looking for direction," he added. "The focus becomes the dollar and what happens from here."
On Thursday, consumer price data and July industrial production and capacity use will be released. Also on tap are June business inventories and July real earnings.

At the close, September T-bonds rose 12/32 to 112-27/32, 10-year notes gained 6/32 to 108-29/32, muni bonds gained 9/32 to 119-2/32, December Eurodollars rallied 0.065 to 94.060, and T-bills added 0.060 to 94.760. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
